reason: Arrow International is not a game studio at all — it is a 1,600-1,700-person Platinum Equity portfolio manufacturer of charitable gambling consumables (pull tabs, bingo paper, ink daubers, electronic bingo cabinets) founded 1967 in Cleveland, so it fails Ben Cole's niche on every axis: wrong vertical (gambling hardware, not PC/console games), wrong side of the market (PE-owned manufacturer, not a funded independent studio), roughly 10x too large for a fractional engagement, and the DevOps/NetOps/SQA postings are ordinary corporate IT and regulatory product-test roles rather than evidence of milestone risk from senior engineers being pulled off a game entering full production.
